### T-586 — Run the schema upgrade through a process that can reach core

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

blong ./index.ts upgrade in realm/blong-agent ends with EAI_AGAIN for hostname rpc-core after the
upgrade block names agent, login, core and access, and only three of the four tables exist
afterwards: agent_session, agent_checkpoint and agent_event are created and agent_answer is missing.
The block was added because the failure before it was the same lookup, so the next step is to run
the intent in a shape that keeps those realms in process — likely without the microservice default —
and then re-check SHOW TABLES. The schema itself is written and type-checks, so this is the
application path rather than the definition.

Fixed by remote.canSkipSocket in the default config; upgrade now exits 0 and all four agent tables
exist.

### T-589 — The resume step of test.agent.session reports resumed false

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

The third step of test.agent.session, anAnswerResumesASuspendedSessionExactlyOnce, fails at its own
assertion: agent.answer.receive answers stored true but resumed false. The precondition is that the
session row reads suspended and its workerId equals this host at the moment the answer arrives, and
the step asserts the suspended status just before it, so the cause is one of two things to check in
that order: whether agent.session.get answers the row with the id it was handed after
agentSessionSuspend edited it, and whether the session the step picks when the pool has no third
ticket is the one it suspended. The other two steps pass: a tick claims, runs three scripted turns,
writes a checkpoint per step and two tool events, and an answered question continues the loop. Add a
probe in the step that reads the session through agent.session.get immediately before
agentAnswerReceive and asserts its status and workerId, so the next run names which of the two it is
instead of guessing.

Cause was test data, not the precondition: the check reported already-stored because the prompt id
was a literal reused across runs. A per-run prompt id and a both-shapes transcript reader made all
four steps pass.

### T-587 — blong-agent still needs the notify adapters and the gateway surface

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

`adapter/notifyRedis.ts` and `adapter/notifyKafka.ts`: `notify.publish` on the way out plus a
`start()` subscription that calls `agent.answer.wake`, with the kafka group id carrying `HOSTNAME`
so every pod receives every message. It needs a broker to be honest about, so it should be written
beside a test that runs one of them, not before. `T-564` wants `gateway/agent/` validations with
`auth: true` for the ticket and session surface, plus the `.http` collection that plays through
`blong-dev proxy`; the handlers now answer `agent.ticket.claim`, `agent.ticket.release`,
`agent.session.get`, `agent.session.run`, `agent.session.resume`, `agent.session.suspend`,
`agent.answer.receive`, `agent.recovery.scan` and `agent.worker.tick`, so a validation file per
method follows the shape of `realm/blong-chat/gateway/`. `T-565` is the hand run that proves the
whole loop: seed a ticket in the fixture pool, run the realm under `integration` (the `local` sim
account is configured there and `workerStart` is false, so the tick is called by hand), then read
`agent.session.get` and `agent.event.find` for the three turns.

### T-590 — The agent plan's remaining work, in the order to take it

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

What is left in plans/agent/plan.md, in the order it should be taken. First `T-574`, the chat seam:
the agent realm cannot load chat's simulators because `realm/blong-chat/package.json` exports only
`./server.ts`, so a child `import('@feasibleone/blong-chat/sim/slackSim.ts')` is blocked by the
exports map. The enabler is one line in that map (the simulator is a reusable test double, like
`@feasibleone/blong-test`), then an agent-side `chat` intent block that lists only `test.agent.chat`
in `watch.test` — that intent separation is required because `questionMethod` is a single port
setting and every other group answers its questions through `test.agent.question.echo`, so a
chat-pointed run must schedule the seam group alone. The group itself starts `agent.session.run`
without awaiting it, polls `agent.checkpoint.last.get` for the pending prompt id, delivers the
answer through `chat.in.answer.receive`, and then awaits the run. Second `T-560`/`T-572`, the notify
adapters: both brokers answer here (6379, 9092) but the Redis adapter has no `pub`/`sub` at all, so
that vocabulary must be added to `core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/redis.ts` before a realm
instance can subscribe; Kafka can carry a wake as a triple today. Third `T-578`/`T-579` (a writable
claim for the workspace, a `dshHome` volume, the key as a Secret) and `T-581`, which needs the
generator driven from a suite — `blong ./index.ts k8s` in the realm exits 0 and writes nothing, so
the realm entry is not the place it runs. Then `T-576`/`T-577` for the coverage number and the
cross-package run, and `T-585` if a blog post is wanted.

the sequence is finished: the chat seam, the notify brokers, the deployment contribution and the
verification are all done; only the optional blog post (T-585) is left

### T-591 — The real-model group proves the loop against a local Ollama

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

test.agent.model is the one group that runs a real model: the ollama intent adds a qwen account of
kind vercel pointed at a LAN Ollama, and the group reads a file, asks for a tool call, writes the
answer back and has those steps replayed from the checkpoint. It is scheduled by the ollama intent
alone, never in integration, because the machine that runs CI has no model: the step keeps its
prompt and its context small (32k) so it stays inside what a local runtime can hold. A provider
package is not needed for any of it — the AI SDK's OpenAI client takes a base URL (D-714) — and the
account differs from a vendor one only in where it points. The base URL lives in the local rc file
rather than in the source, because the address is the machine's and not the realm's.
